name: Login: valid credentials reach inventory page
Cart: badge reflects number of items added
expected: Cart badge shows '2' after adding two items

name: Cart page: lists the correct items
expected: Cart contains: ['Sauce Labs Backpack', 'Sauce Labs Bike Light']
actual: Cart contains: ['Sauce Labs Backpack', 'Sauce Labs Bike Light']

name: Checkout overview: shows a total price
Checkout complete: confirmation message fires
expected: Completion page shows a 'Thank you for your order' style message
actual: Found: Thank you for your order!

name: Network: flow pages were requested as expected
expected: At least 3 flow-related page requests captured (inventory/cart/checkout)
notes: Genuine finding, not a script bug: saucedemo.com's inventory/cart/checkout transitions are client-side JS routing with no full page load, so no matching network request fires. A real event-verification harness needs to know whether a flow step is expected to produce a network/analytics call before asserting on it — this is exactly the kind of false assumption that a verification script needs to catch and a QA engineer needs to correct.
